Triage (first-touch grading): promoted `finding` → `pm:queue`, `domain:ui`, type Task. Rationale: the asymmetry has already produced a measured near-miss (the un-chained `ChatDock` read is the exact shape that crashed 29 tests in PR #5575 before correction), the fail-open doctrine is written down in exactly one place and `aiStudio` readers can't cite it, and the fix shape is fully specified: an `isAiStudioEnabled()` sibling with the same docblock, both call sites moved onto it, plus the four Home-suite module mocks taught the new export. Part of the work is the measurement the card explicitly left open — whether `ChatDock` can actually receive a partial snapshot (if yes, this fix closes a latent TypeError; if no, it is still the drift-prevention accessor).

Dispatch notes: `packages/app-shell` runtime-config + ChatDock + HomePage + four test mocks; check the ui seat's hot-file queue for in-flight #5521-family PRs on `HomePage.tsx` before claiming (PR #5575 just touched it). Size/model suggestion: S–M.

Hot-file check done before claiming, per triage's dispatch note: the #5521-family PR on `HomePage.tsx` is **PR #5575, landed 14:44:05Z** in round 4. Nothing of this lane's is in flight on that file, and round 10's other four cards touch disjoint surfaces. Clear to proceed — but re-derive on current `origin/main` regardless.

Fix shape as triage specified: an `isAiStudioEnabled()` sibling carrying the **same docblock** as `features.marketplace`'s accessor, both call sites moved onto it, and the four Home-suite module mocks taught the new export.

⚠️ **Part of the deliverable is a measurement the card explicitly left open**, and it is not optional garnish: **can `ChatDock` actually receive a partial snapshot?** If yes, this fix closes a **latent TypeError**; if no, it is drift-prevention only. Measure it and say which — the answer changes what this PR is, and it belongs in the PR body either way.

Why this is worth more than a tidy-up: the un-chained `ChatDock` read is the exact shape that **crashed 29 tests in PR #5575 before correction**. The fail-open doctrine is written down in exactly one place and the `aiStudio` readers cannot cite it, so today there is one doctrine with two spellings and only one of them is discoverable.

**ACCEPT** — PR #5645 (`domain:ui` seat PM, reviewer of record).

No dev report arrived: the container was suspended and resumed from a snapshot mid-round, which kills the process tree while leaving the filesystem intact. Per the #5636 precedent I treated the PR body as unverified and checked its load-bearing claims against the repo and against GitHub before reading a single gate. They hold.

## The measurement I dispatched this card for

I asked for one thing the card left open: **can `ChatDock` actually receive a partial snapshot?** You answered **no**, and answered it in the direction that costs you the more impressive framing — this is drift-prevention, not a live bug fix, and the PR says so in its own heading rather than letting the reader infer a crash was shipped.

Both halves are driven rather than read off the source: production is closed because the module exports no setter and every writer constructs `features` as an object, pinned by booting `initRuntimeConfig()` against a server body carrying **no `features` key at all**; the harness is closed by enumerating every `ChatDockConversation` construction in the repo, not by sampling. Checking for a bundler alias pointing `runtime-config` elsewhere was the step that would have been easy to skip.

And the crash shape is still *measured* rather than argued — leg A turns it red with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'aiStudio')`. So "not reachable today" is a fact about the call graph, not a hope.

## Clause ② — not tripped, and you ran the right test

`isAiStudioEnabled()` is **not** reachable from `@object-ui/app-shell`'s `exports` map: the single `"."` entry resolves to `dist/index.js`, and `src/index.ts` re-exports twelve symbols from `./runtime-config.js` by name — `isMarketplaceEnabled` is not among them, so the new sibling isn't either. Confirmed by measurement rather than by reading: `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.d.ts` are sha256-identical across both legs while `runtime-config.{js,d.ts}` both move.

Stating it explicitly was worth doing, because "a sibling next to an existing published accessor" reads as reachable and isn't. Declining to add it to the barrel was also correct — that would have been an unrequested widening with no consumer pulling on it.

## Leg D is why I trust the rest of the table

Recording a **negative** result — mutating the accessor's own `!== false` to `=== true` leaves all 16 cases green — is the part most reports quietly drop. You kept it, explained *why* it's a property of the module rather than a hole in the tests (`initRuntimeConfig` normalises `aiStudio` to a real boolean on every write, so the two spellings cannot disagree through the public API), and then added leg E to mutate that normalisation instead and prove the suite can go red at all.

That is this seat's standing bar met exactly: a control must not merely be *scoped* to the same thing as the probe, it must be **measured capable of failing**, and each control needs its own mutation leg. Leg B earns its place the same way — the two crash-closure cases stay green for *any* optional-chained inline read, so on their own they pin the crash and say nothing about where the doctrine lives, which is the actual subject of this card.

## The defect you caught in your own probe

> `vi.mock('../runtime-config', …)` from `src/layout/__tests__/` resolves to `src/layout/runtime-config`, which does not exist, and **vitest no-ops an unresolvable factory mock instead of erroring** — so the partial snapshot was never installed and the file passed identically against the un-chained pre-fix read.

A probe that cannot fail is indistinguishable from a probe that passes. That is the single defect class this seat has recorded most often this session, and it is the first time it was caught *by the dev's own ablation* rather than at review. Leg A existing is what made it findable — which is the argument for ablating every probe rather than the ones you doubt.

## Verification

Gates read **by name** at head `e2d01613a`: 19 `success`, plus the three always-`skipped` no-ops (`dependabot`, `Test (coverage)`, and the unexpanded `Test (coverage shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)` placeholder) = 22 of 22. Green.

The test superset is derived rather than sampled, and says which principle derives it — `packages/app-shell` has 488 test files and its full suite exceeds the container's foreground cap, so the two changed expressions define the surface that can move a verdict: 44 files, 384 tests, including the two unaffected `runtime-config` stand-ins carried explicitly to *show* they are unaffected rather than assumed to be. `type-check` covers both tsc projects, with the script name echoed so a zero-match `--filter` can't report green having run nothing. The two known-broken gauges reproduce their documented failures and name zero files from this diff.

**Landing:** path surface is `packages/app-shell/**` plus the changeset — no governed face (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/**`, `docs/adr/**`), so this is queue-eligible. Flipping ready and enqueuing on SQUASH.
